route.asbFinancing.heading: Compare leverage, dividends, and direct contributions before you commit to ASB financing.
route.asbFinancing.intro: See how a compounding strategy, a dividend-offset strategy, and direct ASB contributions compare over the same analysis horizon.
route.asbFinancing.assumptions: Assumptions: reducing-balance monthly amortized financing, a fixed annual ASB dividend rate credited once per year, and dividends reinvested unless a strategy explicitly redirects them. All three strategies commit the same monthly cash amount; the dividend-offset strategy tracks freed-up cash in a side investment with its own annual return rate instead of letting it disappear from the comparison. This is a planning projection, not a bank-issued ASBF quote.
route.carLoan.heading: Understand your full repayment cost before you commit to a car loan.
route.carLoan.intro: Compare financed amount, total interest, monthly instalment, and a documented early-settlement estimate in one place.
route.carLoan.assumptions: Assumptions: variable rate (reducing balance, EIR) is the default, reflecting the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026; fixed rate (flat rate with a Rule of 78 style rebate) remains available for legacy comparisons. Early-settlement estimates are optional and off by default. This is a projection tool, not a lender-issued payoff quote.
route.compoundInterest.heading: Model growth with fixed returns and optional monthly contributions.
route.compoundInterest.intro: This calculator uses the documented compound-growth model with a fixed annual rate, configurable compounding frequency, and end-of-period contribution treatment.
route.compoundInterest.assumptions: Assumptions: fixed annual rate across the full duration, annual/monthly/quarterly compounding, and optional monthly contributions applied at the end of each month.
route.propertyInvestment.heading: See whether a rental property or a REIT works harder for the same capital.
route.propertyInvestment.intro: Compare loan balance, rental cash flow, and exit proceeds from a buy-to-rent property against a REIT invested with the same capital over the same holding period.
route.propertyInvestment.assumptions: Assumptions: reducing-balance monthly amortized financing, constant annual rental income and expense assumptions across the holding period, one fixed property exit assumption, and one fixed REIT annual return rate. This is a planning projection, not tax, legal, or investment advice.
route.retirementFund.heading: Project retirement savings and see how long they will last.
route.retirementFund.intro: Model EPF-style contributions through your working years, then simulate a gratuity-and-pension-style withdrawal pattern to see how long the accumulated fund lasts.
route.retirementFund.assumptions: Assumptions: annual return credited once per year on the end-of-year balance, not compounded monthly, matching the ASB financing dividend-crediting convention. Outputs are nominal and do not adjust for inflation, tax, or EPF withdrawal rules. This is planning guidance, not financial advice.
route.salaryCalculator.heading: Break down your gross salary into net take-home pay and employer cost.
route.salaryCalculator.intro: See every statutory deduction - EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB - plus optional Lindung24 protection. Supports Malaysian citizens, permanent residents, and foreign workers.
route.salaryCalculator.assumptions: Uses the latest published EPF, SOCSO, EIS, and PCB rate schedules. Foreign workers use a flat 30% PCB rate and optional EPF. This is planning guidance, not official payroll advice.
asb.strategy.compounding.label: Compounding strategy
asb.strategy.compounding.description: Financed principal stays invested and dividends compound while you pay the full instalment out of pocket.
asb.strategy.dividendOffset.label: Dividend-offset strategy
asb.strategy.dividendOffset.description: Financed principal stays invested. Each month the dividend reserve covers as much of your instalment as it can, carrying forward until depleted, and frees your monthly money into a side investment.
asb.strategy.directContribution.label: Direct ASB strategy
asb.strategy.directContribution.descript: No financing is used. The same monthly instalment amount is contributed directly into ASB instead.

asb.metric.finalAsbValue.definition: Your total ASB unit balance at the end of the analysis horizon, including any dividends reinvested into the account.
asb.metric.cumulativeDividends.definitio: The total dividends generated over the horizon, whether they stayed in ASB or were redirected to pay instalments.
asb.metric.sideInvestmentValue.definitio: Money freed up from your monthly budget by the dividend-offset strategy, grown separately outside your ASB account.
asb.metric.cashPaidByYou.definition: The total amount you paid out of your own pocket over the horizon, not counting money from dividends or financing.
asb.metric.remainingLoanBalance.definiti: How much you would still owe the bank if you stopped at the end of this horizon.
asb.metric.surrenderValue.definition: The amount of your original financing you would get back from the bank if you ended the facility today, before counting any dividend or side-investment profit.
asb.metric.netPosition.definition: Your total financial position if you ended everything today: surrender value plus dividend or side-investment profit.
asb.disclaimer: This comparison applies the documented reducing-balance financing model and annual dividend-crediting assumption from the spec. It is planning guidance, not a bank-issued ASBF quote.

retirement.field.yearsToRetirement.helpe: Whole number of years, at least 1.
retirement.field.annualReturnRate.label: Annual return rate (%)
retirement.field.annualReturnRate.helper: Fixed for the full accumulation horizon, credited once per year.

retirement.summary.heading: Projection Summary
retirement.metric.finalCapital.definitio: The ending retirement savings balance at the close of the last projection year, after the final year's return is credited.
retirement.metric.totalContributions.def: The cumulative sum of every monthly contribution paid in across all years, including both employee and employer portions.
retirement.metric.totalGrowth.definition: Final capital minus the initial savings balance minus total contributions - the portion of the ending balance that came from investment return alone.
retirement.metric.timeToDepletion.defini: How long the retirement fund lasts under the entered withdrawal pattern before the balance reaches zero, or a report that it does not deplete within 100 years.
retirement.summary.note: Annual return credited once per year on the end-of-year balance; contributions accumulate monthly throughout each year.
retirement.scenario.staysInvested.label: Stays invested
retirement.scenario.staysInvested.descri: The remaining balance stays invested and continues to earn the post-retirement return rate, credited once per year, while monthly withdrawals continue every month.
retirement.scenario.fullyWithdrawn.label: Fully withdrawn
retirement.scenario.fullyWithdrawn.descr: The entire sum is withdrawn into cash. No investment return continues to accrue; the balance simply decreases by the monthly withdrawal each month.
retirement.field.startingBalance.label: Starting balance (RM)
retirement.field.startingBalance.helper: Defaults to Section A's final capital; editable directly.
retirement.field.lumpSumWithdrawal.label: Lump-sum withdrawal (RM)
retirement.field.lumpSumWithdrawal.helpe: One-time withdrawal deducted at the start of month 1; may be zero.
retirement.field.monthlyWithdrawal.label: Monthly withdrawal (RM)
retirement.field.monthlyWithdrawal.helpe: Deducted every month starting month 1; may be zero.
retirement.field.postRetirementAnnualRet: Applies to the stays-invested scenario only; separate from Section A's rate.
retirement.footerNote: Month 1 deducts the lump-sum withdrawal and the first monthly withdrawal together. The simulation runs for a maximum of 100 years (1,200 months).

salary.metric.grossMonthlySalary.definit: Your total monthly base salary before any statutory deductions or contributions.
salary.metric.epfEmployee.definition: Your mandatory contribution to the Employees Provident Fund. The rate is typically 11% of your monthly salary for employees under 60.
salary.metric.epfEmployer.definition: Your employer's mandatory contribution to your EPF account. The rate is typically 12-13% depending on your salary level and age.
salary.metric.socso.definition: Social Security Organization contributions under the Employment Injury Scheme and Invalidity Scheme. Provides coverage for work-related injuries and invalidity.
salary.metric.eis.definition: Employment Insurance System (Sistem Insurans Pekerjaan) contributions. Provides employment protection and retrenchment benefits for eligible workers.
salary.metric.pcb.definition: Potongan Cukai Bulanan (Monthly Tax Deduction). Monthly income tax deducted at source based on your chargeable income after EPF relief.
salary.metric.lindung24.definition: Optional PERKESO voluntary protection scheme providing 24-hour coverage for accidents and illnesses beyond work-related incidents. Coverage capped at RM6,000 monthly salary.
salary.metric.netTakeHome.definition: Your gross salary minus all statutory deductions and optional contributions. This is the amount you actually receive in your bank account.
salary.metric.totalEmployerCost.definiti: The total amount your employer pays for your employment: gross salary plus all employer statutory contributions (EPF, SOCSO, EIS).
